ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached diagram shows a large rectangle divided into a 5-by-6 grid, so there are 30 equal small squares. Reading the grey squares by row from top to bottom: row 1 has columns 2 through 6 grey; row 2 has columns 1 through 4 grey; row 3 has columns 2 and 4 grey; row 4 has columns 2 and 4 through 6 grey; row 5 has columns 4 through 6 grey. Reasoning: Count the exposed unit-square edges around the grey region, including edges next to white squares and edges on the outside of the big rectangle. The big rectangle contains 30 such squares, so its area is 30 × 8^2 = 30 × 64 = 1920 cm^2.

method.method_draft: First read the image as a 5-by-6 array and list the grey squares. Count 18 grey squares total. Then count shared sides between adjacent grey squares: 11 horizontal shared sides within rows and 10 vertical shared sides between rows, for 21 shared sides total. Use the polyomino perimeter formula: if N unit squares form the grey area and S pairs of adjacent grey squares share a side, then the grey perimeter in unit edges is 4N - 2S. Thus the grey perimeter is 4×18 - 2×21 = 30 unit edges. From the text, 30 unit edges equal 240 cm, so one square side is 8 cm. Since the big rectangle has 30 equal squares, its area is 30×8^2 = 1920 cm^2.
